question: What identity is being assigned to the soul by equating the more supreme one with Haṃsa as power-individual?
premises: The soul is indicated as that entity.
That entity is said to be more supreme.
The relative clause identifies which one is meant.
That same entity is called Haṃsa, described as power-individual.
inference: The soul is the more supreme entity who is Haṃsa, the power-individual.
uncertainties: Technical sense of śakti+pudgala not determined by this verse alone
plain_english: He is the soul, more supreme; he indeed is Haṃsa, the power-individual.
